styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Met, MoMA, Broadway and the old downtown streets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Bagels, pizza slices, Chinatown and a steakhouse night.

styles.label: Views
styles.blurb: Skyline decks, bridges and the Staten Island Ferry.

stays.why: Walk to Times Square, Central Park and Grand Central. Best for first-timers and short trips. Noisy and busy.
Near the Statue of Liberty ferry, Wall Street and the Brooklyn Bridge. Quiet at night on weekends.
Next to Central Park and the Natural History Museum. Calmer, family-friendly, good subway links.
Brooklyn Bridge Park, DUMBO and cheaper rooms. 20–30 minutes to Midtown by subway.

food: Start with a New York breakfast: a bagel with cream cheese and lox, or a bodega egg sandwich, about $8–15.
Grab a pizza slice for $4–6. Sit-down dinners run $30–60 a person before drinks.
Chinatown and Flushing have the best cheap eats: dumplings, noodles and roast meats for $10–20.
Food halls and markets (Chelsea Market, Essex Market) let a group split up and eat cheaply.
Book popular dinner spots a few days ahead. Many places add tax and tip on top of menu prices.
more_time: Swap a Midtown day for Brooklyn: walk the Brooklyn Bridge, then DUMBO and Brooklyn Bridge Park.
Add a half-day at the American Museum of Natural History or the Met. Both need 3–4 hours.
Take the free Staten Island Ferry for skyline and Statue of Liberty views, then ride back.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the big museums, a skyline view and a Brooklyn walk without rushing.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 4°C, lows around -3°C. Pack a warm coat and layers.
Still cold, highs about 6°C. Good for museums and indoor sights.
Warming up to 10°C. Some rain; a light jacket works.
Spring: highs around 16°C, lows 6°C. Comfortable for walking.
Pleasant at 21°C. Busy with tourists; book hotels early.
Warm at 26°C. Good park weather; expect about 11 rain days.
Hottest month: highs near 30°C, lows 21°C. Plan shade and water.
Hot and humid, highs around 28°C. Evenings are best for walking.
Still warm at 25°C. A great month for parks and rooftops.
Cool and clear, highs near 19°C. Good for long walks.
Colder at 12°C. Fewer rain days; pack a jacket.
Cold again: highs about 7°C, lows near 0°C. Holiday crowds in December.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons. Hot, humid summers and cold winters. Spring and autumn are the best times to walk the city.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Highs of 16–26°C. Comfortable for walking and parks. These are the busiest months.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (July to August)
items.text: Highs near 28–30°C with muggy nights. Plan indoor sights at midday and walk in the morning or evening.

items.title: Winter is cold (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 4–7°C and lows near or below 0°C. Bring a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain is spread through the year
items.text: About 8–13 rain days a month. April and July are the wettest. Carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Autumn is crisp and clear
items.text: October highs near 19°C and fewer rain days. Great for parks and skyline views.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers, a rain jacket and sunscreen for summer. A warm coat for winter.

transit.best: The subway for most trips; walk Manhattan's grid for short hops.

modes.text: The subway runs 24 hours. Tap OMNY (contactless) for $3.00 a ride, with a weekly fare cap.
Buses use the same fare. The M-routes cover Manhattan avenues.
Yellow cabs are metered (plus congestion surcharges). Uber and Lyft work everywhere.
Driving and parking in Manhattan are slow and expensive. Skip the car.
Manhattan's grid is easy to walk. 20 blocks north-south is about a mile.
The free Staten Island Ferry passes the Statue of Liberty.
